short: England's first ruling queen, and the last attempt to restore Catholicism.
full:
Mary took the throne in July 1553 on a wave of popular support against Jane Grey's proclamation, the first woman to rule England in her own right. She restored the Latin mass, reunited the church with Rome under Cardinal Pole in 1554, and repealed her father's and brother's religious legislation, though she could not recover the monastic lands from their new owners.

Her marriage to Philip of Spain in 1554 was unpopular enough to provoke Wyatt's rebellion, and the treaty terms were written to keep England out of Habsburg hands. From 1555 the heresy laws were enforced hard: some 280 people were burned, among them Cranmer, Latimer and Ridley, and John Foxe's account of them shaped English Protestant identity for centuries. War alongside Spain cost England Calais, its last continental possession, in January 1558. Mary died childless that November, and her half-sister Elizabeth undid the settlement within a year.
